paper_title: New ALPS Results on Hidden-Sector Lightweights
coupling_convention: g_agamma in GeV^-1 (square root of conversion probability limits)
notes: Paper presents LSW (Light Shining through a Wall) experiment results constraining axion-like particles (ALPs), hidden photons, and mini-charged particles. For ALPs, the conversion probability P(γ↔φ) is related to coupling g± via Eq. (5). The 95% C.L. limits on conversion probabilities from Table 1 are converted to coupling limits via P ∝ (g·ω·B·cos θ)²/M⁴. The most stringent constraints come from vacuum runs (n≡1). Data points represent approximate g_agamma values extracted from the conversion probability limits (few ×10^-25) using the experimental parameters: ω=2.33 eV, B=5 T, l=8.8 m. The paper also constrains hidden photons (kinetic mixing χ) and mini-charged particles, but the primary new laboratory limits are on ALPs. Figure 4 shows exclusion limits for both pseudoscalar (g⁻) and scalar (g⁺) ALPs across the sub-eV mass range, with best sensitivity in the meV region. The coupling values are mass-dependent but the paper does not provide explicit tabulated (mass, coupling) pairs; the data points above represent approximate horizontal bands from the vacuum measurements at different configurations. | selector: table (sole candidate)
